title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

chapters.title: How you fall
chapters.teaser: Fast, slow, sideways or all at once. The way your soul actually falls for someone.

chapters.title: Your flirting style
chapters.teaser: What you think you're doing, what they think you're doing, and the one move that lands.

chapters.title: Your attachment pattern
chapters.teaser: Clingy, cool, steady or somewhere in between. How you hold on when you care.

chapters.title: Jealousy and your trigger
chapters.teaser: The exact thing that sets you off, and what you do instead of saying it.

chapters.title: Yeon's red flag report
chapters.teaser: The love habit you keep repeating. Yeon does not soften this chapter.

chapters.title: What you actually need
chapters.teaser: Not your type. Your match. The kind of person and love that lets you relax.

text.how-you-fall: You fall sideways. Eul is the vine and the wildflower, and vines don't charge at things, they wind. One day you're just friends, the next you've memorized their coffee order, their sister's name and the exact playlist that fixes their bad days, and you realize you've been falling for weeks. You attach through closeness and small daily contact. Texting good morning, sharing memes, borrowing their hoodie. It's gentle and it's sneaky, even to you. The beauty of this is that your love feels natural and easy, never forced. The risk is that you can wrap yourself around a person before you've checked whether they're a strong trellis or a wobbly fence post. You adapt to fit them so well that it's hard to tell, later, which parts of you were yours.
text.flirting: You are a natural. Flirting is basically your second language, and most of the time you don't even know you're doing it. The tilted head, the "wait, tell me more," the way you remember a detail they mentioned once and bring it up three days later. People feel seen around you, and that's the whole trick. You also flirt in groups beautifully, drawing the quiet one into the conversation so they think you're the warmest person alive. The downside: people sometimes can't tell if you're into them or just being you. If you actually like someone, make it unmistakable once. Ask them to something with just the two of you, and name it. "I'd like to take you to that ramen place. Like a date." Vines are allowed to be direct.
text.attachment: Your attachment pattern leans anxious when you care a lot. You read the temperature of a relationship constantly: a shorter reply, a missing emoji, a slight change in how they say your name. You're very good at adjusting to keep the peace, which looks like flexibility but can become disappearing. You'd rather bend than risk a fight, so needs go unsaid and slowly build into a quiet resentment you don't fully show. When you feel secure, though, you are one of the most delightful partners there is: playful, affectionate, socially easy, great at weaving someone into your life and friends. The work for you is noticing the moment you start shrinking to keep someone comfortable. That's your cue to say one true thing, even if your voice shakes a little.
text.jealousy: Your jealousy is social. You're not threatened by a stranger, you're threatened by the friend who seems to get them in a way you don't, the coworker with all the inside jokes, the ex they still laugh with. Because connection is your superpower, someone else's connection with your person can feel like a direct competitor. And you're too graceful to make a scene, so you do something worse: you become extra charming, extra helpful, extra easy, trying to win a contest nobody announced. Then you're exhausted. The healthier move is curiosity instead of competition. Ask, lightly, "you two seem close, what's the story?" Most of the time the answer is boring. And when it isn't, at least you'll know, instead of shapeshifting in the dark.
text.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you lose your shape. You become the version of yourself that fits whoever you're dating. With the indie musician you suddenly own vinyl. With the gym person you're up at six. It's charming for a while, and then you look in the mirror and can't remember what you liked before them. Second flag: you avoid conflict so skillfully that problems grow roots under the floorboards. You say "it's fine" with a smile so convincing you almost believe it. Third, smaller one: you keep options open. A little flirting with the backup plan, just in case. You don't mean harm, you just hate the feeling of having nowhere to go. Pick a trellis you actually trust, then stop hedging.
text.what-you-need: You need a partner who is genuinely sturdy. Someone calm and consistent, who doesn't swing between hot and cold, so you can stop reading the weather and just grow. You need to be adored out loud, often, in small ways: a text in the afternoon, a hand on your back at a party, being introduced proudly. You also need someone who wants your real opinions, not your agreeable ones, and who keeps asking until they get them. Space matters too, oddly. Vines need to climb, and your friendships, hobbies and little side quests are not a threat to love, they're what keeps you interesting. The best match for you holds steady while you move, and is delighted, not threatened, when you bloom in a direction they didn't predict.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, you love like a vine. Gentle, close, woven into every little part of their day.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And by month three you've adopted their music taste, their friends and their opinions on cilantro.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're just so adaptable! People feel completely seen by you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: People feel seen. You feel invisible. Fun trade.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say one true thing out loud this week. Your real opinion is part of your charm.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: "It's fine" is not a love language. Stop saying it.

spring.intro: Spring-born Eul Wood is the vine in full bloom, in season and very aware of it. You flirt the way flowers open, gradually and then all at once, and you are excellent at reading what the other person wants and becoming the version of you that fits. That adaptability makes you easy to fall for. In love, though, a strong Eul in spring can wrap around a person until neither of you remembers where you end. You don't grip like Gap. You twine. Metal, the element that controls Wood, is your teacher here: a clear boundary, a separate weekend, an opinion you keep even when theirs is louder. Flowers need a trellis, not another flower.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Eul, you agreed with their music, their politics and their opinion of their ex. Pick one.

summer.intro: In summer, Fire takes the wheel and Wood becomes its fuel, so a summer-born Eul Wood gives off a lot of light for a delicate plant. You are charming in a sunny, sociable way: the person who sends the funny voice note, remembers their best friend's birthday, and makes every date photogenic. You express love generously and visibly. The trouble with summer flowers is that they droop in the afternoon heat. You can give so much attention that you feel quietly empty, then start keeping score in your head instead of asking for what you need. Water is your resource, and in love it looks like reassurance. Ask for it directly. Drooping hints never work as well as words.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Eul, you water everyone else's garden. Saying 'I'd love a little attention' is allowed.

autumn.intro: Autumn is Metal's season, and Metal cuts Wood. For a delicate Eul Wood, that means arriving in a season of pruning, so you learned early to bend instead of breaking. In love you are perceptive and careful. You notice the tone of a text before you notice the words, and you adapt fast to keep the peace. Many autumn Eul lovers end up with someone strong, decisive, a little bossy, and call it chemistry. Sometimes it is. Sometimes it is a familiar pressure. The question for you is not whether you can survive someone's sharp edges. You obviously can. It is whether you should have to. Partners who are gentle and firm at once do exist.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Eul, 'they're intense but they mean well' is not a love language. It's an excuse.

winter.intro: Winter hands command to Water. It nourishes Wood, but frost is hard on a flowering vine, so a winter-born Eul Wood is resourceful, observant and slightly guarded. You read people beautifully, sometimes too beautifully, and you can talk yourself out of a crush before it starts because you have already imagined the ending. Your love is patient. You will wait out a slow season with someone and stay soft while you do it. What you lack is sun. Fire, your output element, shows up as play, flirting, being a little silly on purpose. Someone warm and openly affectionate thaws you faster than any amount of logic, and you deserve love that feels like a sunny windowsill.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Eul, you're not cold. You're waiting for someone warm enough. Let them find the window.

earth.intro: Born in the Earth days, Eul, you're a vine growing over firm ground. Wood controls Earth, so you love by weaving yourself into someone's life: their routines, their friends, their favorite places. It's tender, and it's quietly strategic. You get close without ever asking for closeness. The risk is that you lose your own shape inside theirs. You need a partner who notices what you want before you've adapted away from it. Tell them, early and plainly.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Eul, you blend in so well they forget to ask what you'd like. Tell them.

strength.strong: A strong Eul Wood is a vine with a whole wall to climb. Plenty of Wood and Water in your chart makes you persuasive, persistent and very good at getting your way gently. In love you can steer a partner without them noticing, nudging plans, moods and decisions until things go your direction. Your blind spot is soft control: never demanding, always arranging. It works until your partner feels quietly handled and cannot say why. Try asking directly for what you want and accepting a no without working around it. Your charm is real. It is most powerful when it is honest about where it is leading.
strength.weak: A weak Eul Wood is a delicate plant in thin soil, and you know it. With little Wood or Water support in your chart, you bend too easily in love. You mirror a partner's moods, adopt their friends and hobbies, and apologize for things that were never your fault. Your blind spot is over-giving to stay close, as though love must be earned with flexibility. Over time you can lose track of your own taste entirely. Practice one small preference a day: the restaurant, the film, the night in. People who love you will be delighted to finally know what you think.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood in your chart turns love into a growth plan. You want things to move forward, define the relationship, make progress, and slow phases make you restless. You can also be stubborn in arguments, holding your position like a tree in wind. In love this looks like big intentions and a little impatience. Balance it with Metal energy: clear agreements, pruning what isn't working, and accepting that some things are already finished growing. Not every relationship needs to become a forest. Some are perfect as a single, steady tree.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means beginnings are your hard part. You might hold back until someone else makes the first move, define things, or suggest the next step, and you can stay in a comfortable but stuck situation for too long. Your love is real, it just doesn't push. Balance it by practicing small starts: suggest the date, send the first text, say what you hope for out loud. Green things help as reminders, a plant by your bed, a green phone case. Love grows when someone plants it. Sometimes that someone is you.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your love bright, fast and a little combustible. You fall hard and feel everything at full volume, whether you show it out loud or keep it behind your eyes. The highs are glorious. The lows, when attention drops, feel like the lights went out. You can also lose interest once the excitement settles. Balance it with Water energy: slowing down, letting quiet evenings count, and sitting with feelings before reacting. Ask yourself if you love the person or the thrill. The best flame for you burns steady, not just bright.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means passion and visibility don't come easily in love. You might care deeply but struggle to show it, hold back affection until you're sure, or feel awkward with romantic gestures. People can mistake your reserve for disinterest. Balance it by letting warmth out in small, brave doses: a compliment, a hug that lasts a second longer, a little playfulness. Warm colors and sunlight help you feel more expressive. You don't need fireworks. You just need people to see that the light is on.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth makes you a steady, devoted partner who can get a little stuck. You value security, routine and loyalty, and you might stay in familiar patterns even when they've stopped making you happy. Change feels risky. You may also over-care, taking on your partner's problems as your own. Balance it with Wood energy: try something new together, plan an adventure, let the relationship grow in surprising directions. Safe is wonderful. Safe and alive is even better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means love can feel unsteady. You might worry about where things stand, struggle to settle into commitment, or jump between highs and lows. You can also find it hard to trust that someone will stay. Balance it by building small, reliable rituals: a weekly date, a regular call, a shared routine. Choose partners who are consistent rather than exciting. Earth tones and home-cooked meals help you feel grounded. Stability isn't boring. For you, it's what lets love feel safe enough to enjoy.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives you strong standards and very clear boundaries in love. You know what you want and what you won't tolerate, which is healthy, until it becomes rigid. You can be critical, quick to judge, or end things abruptly when disappointed. Balance it with Fire energy: warmth, forgiveness, play. Let small mistakes be small. Say the kind thing before the honest thing. Strong boundaries keep you safe. Soft edges let people actually come close enough to love you.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are your hard part in love. You might say yes when you mean no, stay too long, or let people treat you less well than you deserve because you don't want conflict. Your heart is open, sometimes too open. Balance it by practicing clear, simple limits: "I'm not okay with that," without a long explanation. Decluttering and white or silver accents can help you feel sharper. Boundaries aren't walls. They're the frame that makes the picture of your love clear.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water makes your love deep, intuitive and sometimes overwhelming. You feel everything, read every mood and can get lost in emotional currents or imagined stories. You may also avoid commitment, drifting rather than choosing. Balance it with Earth energy: grounding conversations, practical plans, partners who are steady and clear. Write down what actually happened before reacting to what you feel happened. Your depth is beautiful. It just needs a shore so you don't get swept away.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means emotional depth and rest don't come easily in love. You might stay busy, keep conversations practical, or struggle to sit with vulnerable feelings, yours or your partner's. Love can feel like a to-do list. Balance it with slow, quiet moments: late talks, journaling, listening without fixing. Navy and black, water by your bed, and slow evenings help you soften. You don't need to drown in feelings. Just let yourself wade in a little deeper.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you want it defined, labeled and growing by Thursday. Breathe.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your hope is beautiful. Let it grow at the speed of a real person.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: you fall hard and fast, out loud or in silence. Then the second act bores you.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is a gift. Let it simmer a while. Slow love tastes better.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: staying somewhere stale because leaving takes effort isn't loyalty. It's inertia.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Make sure it's going somewhere that still feeds you.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: your dating checklist has forty points. Nobody passes. Including you.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Standards protect you. Leave one door open for someone surprising.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: you wrote a whole love story in your head. They've read none of it.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is gorgeous. Share a little of it with the real person.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Love won't start itself. Send the first text. Plant something.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Waiting for them to make the move isn't patience. It's hiding behind a nice word.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? Your love is real, it just whispers. Let someone hear it.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: A compliment you only think doesn't count. Say it, then survive the blushing.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? You love brightly but drift. A small weekly ritual keeps you anchored.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Three crushes, zero follow-through. Pick one and show up twice in a row.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? Your kindness needs a boundary. A no keeps your yes worth something.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Three cancellations and a fourth chance isn't generosity. It's a pattern you're funding.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? You act before you feel. Pause and ask what you actually want.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Over someone in a weekend isn't healing. It's skipping the chapter. Read it.
